chunks: 5603 - Al-Faḍl said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Walīd al-ʿAdanī, the companion of Sufyān, narrated, saying: Abū al-Qāsim al-Kūfī, the companion of Abū Yūsuf, narrated to me from Abū Yūsuf, who said: Layth ibn Abī Sulaym narrated to us from Abū ʿAmr al-ʿAbdī, from Ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, that he used to say:

"The obligatory shares are out of six portions: two-thirds are four portions, one-half is three portions, one-third is two portions, one-fourth is one and a half portions, and one-eighth is three-quarters of a portion. None inherits along with the child except the two parents, the husband, and the wife. Nothing prevents the mother from one-third except the child and the siblings. The husband is not increased above one-half, nor reduced from one-fourth. The wife is not increased above one-fourth, nor reduced from one-eighth. If they are four or fewer than that, then they are equal in it. The maternal siblings are not increased above one-third, nor reduced from one-sixth, and in that the male and the female are equal. Nothing prevents them from one-third except the child and the father. The blood money is divided among those who have secured the inheritance."

key_terms.الثُّلُثَانِ: two-thirds as a legal inheritance portion
key_terms.الثُّمُنُ: one-eighth as a fixed inheritance share
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money compensation for killing, distributed as inheritable property
key_terms.النِّصْفُ: one-half as a fixed inheritance share
key_terms.الْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: maternal siblings who inherit under specific rules

ai.seo_question: What are the fixed shares of inheritance in this hadith from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines fixed inheritance shares and the principles governing who inherits in the presence of children, parents, spouses, and maternal siblings. It also states that blood money is distributed according to the same inheritable entitlement, making it a key legal text in the law of inheritance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5603 - Al-Faḍl narrated that Abdullah ibn Al-Walid Al-Adani, the companion of Sufyan, reported from Abu Al-Qasim Al-Kufi, the companion of Abu Yusuf, who narrated from Abu Yusuf, who said: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Abu Amr Al-Abdi, from Ibn Sulayman, from Imam Ali ibn Abi Ṭalib (as), who used to say:

"The shares of inheritance are from six portions: two-thirds is four portions, half is three portions, one-third is two portions, one-fourth is one and a half portions, and one-eighth is three-fourths of a portion.
No one inherits alongside the children except the parents, the husband, and the wife. The mother is not prevented from receiving one-third except by the presence of children or siblings.
The husband's share does not exceed half, nor is it reduced from one-fourth.
The wife's share does not exceed one-fourth, nor is it reduced from one-eighth.
If there are four wives or fewer, they share equally.
Siblings from the mother do not inherit more than one-third and are not given less than one-sixth, and in this, males and females are equal. They are not prevented from receiving one-third except by the presence of children or the father.
Blood money (diyyah for accidental death) is distributed among those who inherit the estate."
